Apex Industrial Dynamics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Dynamics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Dynamics' results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Harper, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Bradley, Chief Operating Officer; and Nina Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Reynolds.

Mark Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Dynamics' performance for the third quarter. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. We've substantially shortened lead times for our key products and components, enhancing customer satisfaction and backlog conversion in this cyclical sector. Demand trends remain strong across our core end markets like construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing, driving robust order growth. We're raising our operating margin guidance for the next quarter and full year, reflecting pricing power and efficiency gains. We've executed disciplined M&A activity to bolster our portfolio and capabilities. Inventory levels are well-managed, supporting working capital optimization. Finally, order intake expectations are solid, with improving backlog conversion rates providing revenue visibility.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Harper to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Harper (CFO):
Thank you, Mark. Turning to our financial performance, Apex Industrial Dynamics reported $1.42 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 32.4%, driven by pricing discipline, favorable product mix, and supply chain efficiencies from our Apex Lean 2.0 initiative. Operating expenses were $450 million, resulting in operating income of $178 million and an operating margin of 12.5%, up 120 basis points year-over-year. Our net income for the quarter was $145 million, or $1.12 per diluted share.

We are managing our capital allocation effectively, prioritizing investments in high-growth areas and returning capital to shareholders through $75 million in share repurchases this quarter.

To give you deeper insight into the drivers behind these results, let me start with lead times for our key products and components—a critical factor for customer satisfaction, backlog conversion, and free cash flow in our industrial equipment business. Our book-to-bill ratio stands at a healthy 1.25x this quarter, improved from 1.15x last year. We've overcome past challenges like the semiconductor shortages and steel disruptions that impacted peers such as Caterpillar and Deere. Through our Resilient Supply Chain 2.0 initiative, we've made major strides.

For our Precision Machining Centers, like the high-speed 5-axis CNC mills in our MDX-500 series used in aerospace and EV battery tooling, average lead times are now 14 weeks, a 30% reduction from 20 weeks in Q3 2023 and 45% from the 26-week peak in late 2022. This comes from a 25% increase in domestic casting capacity at our Ohio facility, cutting reliance on overseas foundries affected by China's policies.

Heavy-duty Automated Material Handling Systems, including next-gen AGVs and palletizers comparable to Dematic or KION Group offerings, are at 16 weeks—a 20% year-over-year improvement. Electronic components like PLCs and servo motors have normalized to 8-10 weeks from 18 weeks, via dual-sourcing with TSMC and Intel facilities in the U.S. and Malaysia. Our vision-guided robotics have de-risked 15% of bill-of-materials costs from single Asian suppliers.

For components such as hydraulic cylinders, linear actuators, and forged steel gears, aggregate lead times are 9 weeks, down 35% year-over-year. Steel specifically improved from 12 to 6 weeks after the U.S. Steel-Nippon deal, stabilizing prices at $850 per ton versus last year's $1,200 volatility. Rare earth magnets for electro-permanent tooling dropped to 11 weeks from 22, through partnerships like MP Materials in California, leveraging IRA incentives.

Regionally, North America (45% of backlog) averages 12 weeks, supported by $150 million capex in Mexico for nearshoring, similar to John Deere's approach. Europe (30%) is at 18 weeks amid energy costs from the Ukraine situation, but our Siemens digital twin platform has cut two weeks off welding robot deliveries. Asia-Pacific (25%) hit 15 weeks with a Vietnam JV offsetting Taiwan issues, positioning us ahead of Fanuc and Haas in semiconductor expansions.

These gains rest on vertical integration—now 40% in-house for high-margin actuators, up from 20%, adding 300 basis points to gross margins; AI-driven demand sensing via SAP IBP with 92% accuracy, cutting safety stock 18% and freeing $120 million in capital; and supplier diversification to 12 Tier 1 partners with OTIF incentives over 95%, addressing last year's chip issues like those at Honeywell.

We anticipate enterprise-wide compression to 12 weeks by year-end as capacity utilization rises to 92% with our South Carolina CNC plant. This de-risks our $4.5 billion backlog, boosts inventory turns to 4.2x, and supports premium pricing, adding 200 basis points to EBITDA margins.

Shifting to demand trends in our key end markets—construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing—which make up 85% of revenue—we posted 11% year-over-year order growth, lifting backlog 22% to $4.5 billion. This taps infrastructure upgrades, commodity cycles, precision farming, and onshoring automation, despite China construction softness and high interest rates.

Construction (42% of revenue) grew 9%, beating global averages per AECOM indices. North America surged 15% on IIJA's $550 billion through 2026, with data centers boosting telehandlers and forklifts like Caterpillar's boom. Europe +4% via NextGenerationEU, offset by German residential weakness; APAC mixed with India's +18% metro projects countering China's -3%. Our E-Series electric excavators offer 30% better efficiency, and IntelliTrack telematics lifts fleet use 12%; aftermarket parts +14%.

Mining (28%) jumped 14% on copper at $4.50/lb and gold over $2,300/oz. Surface equipment +18%, HAULMAX 300-ton trucks +25%; underground BEV loaders over 500 units shipped, 15% share in BHP/Rio Tinto mines. Australia/Canada +20% on ESG electrification; LatAm +10%, Africa rebounding. $150 million R&D for hydrogen drills positions us versus Sandvik.

Agriculture (15%) +2%, hit by flat incomes (USDA $116 billion U.S.) and weather, but precision ag +12% with AgroGuide AI cutting inputs 20%. North America +5%, Brazil -2%, Europe +3%; aftermarket +7% on aging fleets. New GPS balers target $15 billion hay market.

Manufacturing (15%) +7% on reshoring/Industry 4.0; U.S. +11% per ISM, cobots/AGVs +22% versus Fanuc/ABB; auto +9%. Mexico +16% nearshoring; Europe +5% battery plants. Modular CNCs with IoT cut downtime 18%; $200 million CHIPS Act backlog.

We see +8-10% demand in FY25, led by mining/construction. Margins up 150 bps to 28.2% on 4.5% pricing and electrified mix (22%); $300 million capex for expansions; emissions -25% winning ESG bids.

Next, on operating margin guidance, which many of you have asked about amid macro choppiness. Q3's 12.5% beat our 11.5-12.0% range, from 3.8% pricing, automation mix at 28%, and $45 million cost savings via Apex Lean 2.0, like Fanuc/Haas practices.

For Q4, we guide 13.0-13.5%, up 50-100 bps sequentially, on $1.45-1.50 billion revenue. Tailwinds: 2.5-3.0% pricing in semis/EV tools; aftermarket/services to 32% revenue at 45% margins via Siemens MindSphere; utilization 88-90% with Spartanburg ramp (CHIPS subsidies); digital twins cut scrap 22%, SAP S/4HANA saves $20 million annualized.

Headwinds like 5.2% wage inflation and Red Sea freight +10% are offset. North America ~15% margins on IIJA; Europe 10% but rebounding; APAC 16% on semis/solar.

Full year raised to 12.8-13.2% on $5.75-5.85 billion revenue, EPS $4.85-5.05; $110 million cost-outs, gross margins 31.8%, SG&A 19%. FY25 targets 14%+ on automation, reshoring, 40% services via ApexGuard.

Turning to M&A activity, a key to our strategy amid disruptions, labor issues, and Industry 4.0. We've closed two $1.2 billion bolt-ons YTD, third pending; accretive $0.45 EPS FY24, funding 12-15% growth. $800 million cash ops, $400 million 4.2% debt; leverage 1.8x.

$650 million EuroValve Dynamics (Germany) adds €220 million revenue, 22% EBITDA at 8.5x—cryogenic valves for LNG/hydrogen align with REPowerEU/IRA; $12 million synergies, cross-sell to U.S. power gen.

$550 million RoboForge Automation (U.S.) adds $150 million, 18% growth at 7x; ML cobots boost Apex SmartFactory IoT/5G; 15% throughput gains for EV suppliers.

Diversifies EMEA to 25%, NA onshoring +35% inquiries. Ties to electrification ($1.2T capex), AI 45% CAGR, resilience (60% components secured). Pipeline $3-4B; divested foundries $180 million, 18% ROIC.

On inventory levels and strategies, Q3 end at $1.28 billion, +3% QoQ but -8% YoY; DIO 82 days vs. 92 industry (S&P), turns 4.6x vs. 4.4x peers. Raw 38%/$487M -12% YoY; WIP 32%/$410M stable; FG 30%/$383M -15%.

Peaked mid-2023 on chips; destocked legacy, built EV safety stock. NA 75 DIO ($704M); Europe 90 ($320M); APAC 70 ($256M). SAP/Blue Yonder cuts errors 30%; Dynatrack IoT speeds counts 15%; VMI 40% steel; JIT 60%; blockchain pilot targets 10% DIO cut. FCF $285M.

Finally, order intake and backlog conversion: Q3 $1.28 billion +14%, backlog $4.7 billion +21%, 2.3x run-rate, book-to-bill 1.25x. Conversion 87% quarterly, 82% TTM > peers. 0-6 month $2.1B at 92%.

NA 42%/$540M +19% IIJA/EV; Europe 28%/$360M +5%; APAC 25%/$320M +25% semis/PLI. Digital Thread +15% accuracy; reshoring de-risks 30%; ESG 18% intake.

Q4 intake $1.3-1.4B, FY25 mid-teens; conversion 80-85%.

These metrics position us strongly. Next, to Tom for operations.

Tom Bradley (COO):
Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've focused on productivity across facilities, implementing lean principles and data analytics for process optimization. Supply chain resilience investments, including nearshoring, have been key. Utilization is at 85%, trending higher.

I'll turn the call over to Nina Patel, our CTO, for a technology update.

Nina Patel (CTO):
Thank you, Tom. We're driving innovation with R&D in AI, machine learning, and IoT. Our new Apex SmartFactory platform is delivering early results, with 20% productivity gains and 15% downtime reduction for customers. These technologies will reshape industrial operations, creating major opportunities for Apex Industrial Dynamics.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the growth drivers in your digital solutions business?

Nina Patel (CTO):
Thanks, John. Our digital solutions, centered on the Apex SmartFactory platform, are accelerating thanks to integrations like digital twins and predictive maintenance, pulling from our RoboForge acquisition's ML cobots. Demand is surging in manufacturing and semis, with 22% order growth for AGVs and cobots. Features like real-time anomaly detection deliver 15-22% throughput improvements, as in EV pilots. Recurring software revenue is rising to 15% of mix at 85% margins, aligned with Gartner's 45% industrial AI CAGR. We're embedding this across CNCs and handling systems, winning CHIPS Act deals—positioning us versus ABB and Fanuc.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for expanding your presence in emerging markets?

Mark Reynolds (CEO):
Great question, Emily. Emerging markets like India, Vietnam, and Mexico are priorities, representing growth engines. We've invested in a Vietnam JV for components, capturing semis from TSMC/Samsung, and Mexico nearshoring with $150 million capex, mirroring Deere. India's PLI scheme drove $150 million in grinder orders; APAC intake +25%. Risks like China property are offset by diversification—25% APAC revenue with 16% margins. M&A pipeline targets tuck-ins there, leveraging onshoring tailwinds for 10-15% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson (Barclays):
How are you addressing the skilled labor shortage in the manufacturing sector?

Tom Bradley (COO):
Mike, labor shortages are industry-wide, but we're proactive. We've launched workforce programs with $50 million in training for CNC, robotics, and AGV ops, partnering with community colleges and unions. Upskilling 5,000 employees via VR simulations cut onboarding 40%. Incentives tie 4% raises to productivity; automation offsets 20% of needs. Reshoring adds local talent pools in Ohio/South Carolina. ESG focus attracts millennials—our programs boosted retention 15%, supporting 92% utilization ramp.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Mark Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Dynamics. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
